title: Phase 2 triangulator signals — generator-shape and sibling-context
description:
Promoted from: /Users/hugh/github/meridian-online/finetype/orbit/cards/0016-phase-2-triangulator-signals.yaml

Goal: Determine empirically whether 4-signal triangulation lifts non_unknown@0.7 toward the original 60% target on the measure half of failure_log.tsv. If yes — ship Phase 2 and restore ac-02 to 60%. If no — document the structural ceiling in a Phase 2 MADR, leaving ac-02 at the recalibrated 5% floor. Either way the cliff at threshold 0.5 must visibly lift — that is the falsifiable claim that the new signals carry information.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] ac-01 [gate]: Phase 2 plausibility memo — before any Phase 2 signal-implementation code lands, a memo (in progress.md or a spec-adjacent doc) quantifies the fraction of Phase 1's failing rows (those scoring <0.7 under locked Phase 1 weights) that each new signal can plausibly recover. Decomposes by mechanism: rows with neutral header (header_match <0.3) + shape-uniform values (generator-shape addressable); rows with strong sibling-cluster signal regardless of header (sibling-context addressable). Per-signal lift estimates MUST be cited verbatim in ac-03's weight rationale and ac-04's outcome framing — the memo's content is load-bearing for downstream design choices, not a back-fillable artefact. If neither signal alone is estimated to recover ≥25 pp lift, the modal expectation is outcome (b) of ac-04 and the implementation effort is to confirm the structural ceiling.
- [x] ac-02 [gate]: MADR 0085 — "May the inference module consume model-internal sibling-context attention output, given MADR 0083's claim that signals must be independent of the model?" — authored and accepted before any sibling-context signal code lands. Considered options at minimum: (A) Yes, re-frame independence as "independent error sources, not independent code paths"; (B) No, implement sibling-context from scratch in the inference module; (C) Defer Phase 2 sibling-context to a future phase, ship Phase 2 with generator-shape only. Decision rationale must reconcile MADR 0083 lines 105-115. Hard prerequisite — sibling-context implementation is blocked on this MADR.
- [x] ac-03: Phase 2 weight discipline — weights w_v, w_h, w_g, w_s (with w_v + w_h + w_g + w_s = 1.0) LOCKED at design time per a Phase 2 MADR (next available number after 0085) mirroring MADR 0079's discipline. The implementing agent does NOT run a sweep against either calibrate or measure half; weight selection is first-principles reasoning + ac-01 plausibility-memo evidence, not empirical search. Rationale per weight cites (a) first-principles reasoning analogous to MADR 0079's "header > validator because validators are more error-prone" AND (b) per-signal lift estimates from ac-01's memo. Phase 2 weights MADR authored before any signal-implementation code lands.
- [ ] ac-04 [gate]: Empirical floor decision — measured at locked Phase 2 weights on the measure half (10,660 rows, same partition Phase 1 used). One of two outcomes documented in progress.md AND the corresponding deliverable authored: (a) non_unknown@0.7 ≥60% — Phase 2 ships, AND ac-02 in the autonomous-type-inference spec is amended back to 60% in a v1.5 amendment; (b) non_unknown@0.7 <60% — a Phase 2 structural-ceiling MADR (next available number after the weights MADR) names the structural cause AND ac-02 in the autonomous-type-inference spec stays at the 5% recalibrated floor with a cross-reference to the new MADR. Modal expectation is outcome (b) given Phase 1's empirical 7.1% ceiling — outcome (a) requires the new signals to recover 53 pp of structural gap, currently uncharacterised (ac-01 narrows this).
- [ ] ac-05 [gate]: Cliff at threshold 0.5 lifts (falsifiable) — non_unknown rate at threshold 0.5 on the measure half (full 10,660 rows) rises by ≥10 pp absolute over Phase 1's 0.204 baseline (i.e. ≥0.304 measured). This is the load-bearing falsifiable claim that the new signals carry information, independent of whether ac-04 outcome (a) is reached. Sidecar diagnostic (non-gating, reported only): three-threshold trapezoid AUC over [0.5, 0.7] from the full 10,660-row measure half, alongside a recomputed Phase 1 baseline on the same partition (Phase 1's progress.md numbers were computed on a 1000-row deterministic sample, not the full partition); the sidecar is information density for future analysis, not a pass criterion.
- [ ] ac-06 [gate]: Latency budget preserved — median per-column latency stays under 100ms on the 1000-column M1 benchmark inherited from Phase 1's ac-05. Spec includes an auditable cost-model paragraph BEFORE implementation begins, with three concrete components: (i) K (sample count from each generator) pinned to a specific integer; (ii) per-generator µs estimate from a real measurement (e.g. "5 generators sampled from crates/finetype-core/src/generator.rs, mean 80µs each at K=8 ⇒ 240 × 80µs = 19.2ms estimate"); (iii) mitigation triggered up front when (estimated cost) × 1.5 > 30ms remaining headroom (Phase 1 p50 = 70ms; 1.5× safety margin guards under-estimation) — chosen mitigation is one of: precompute generator fingerprints at module load, sub-sample top-N candidates from validator+header pre-filter before generator-shape scan, cache per-column generator-shape across cycles. Sibling-context cost: confirm in writing whether cycle worker's profile call has cached sibling attention output by inference time; if not, model the re-invocation cost analogously.
- [ ] ac-07: Ablation harness + decisive-signal attribution — scripts/bench_infer_floor.py --disable-signal {generator_shape,sibling_context} produces three result tables (full / no-G / no-S). Sidecar gains a `decisive_signal` column ∈ {validator, header, generator_shape, sibling_context, none} = "the signal whose subscore was numerically largest at argmax". Predictability criterion — these are EXPLORATORY TARGETS per MADR 0084 methodology lesson "(b) unbacked target annotation": no prior signal-attribution baseline exists; Phase 2 is itself the first measurement. Hypothesis: no-G regressions concentrate ≥60% by row count in shape-driven types (UUIDs, ISO dates, code-formatted IDs); no-S regressions concentrate ≥60% in neutral-header columns (header_match score <0.3 against argmax type). A high concentration confirms signal orthogonality; a low concentration tells us the new signals are not as orthogonal as hoped — informative either way, no auto-fail.
- [ ] ac-08: Phase 1 infrastructure stable + schema migration + cascade rule additions — introduce inference_signals_v2.tsv (15-col: existing 12 + generator_shape + sibling_context + decisive_signal). Phase 1's inference_signals.tsv is frozen per H08 append-only invariant; never rewritten. Cycle worker writes to v2 from Phase 2 onward. CLI flags backward-compatible. Canonical-email smoke test still passes (mechanism = prediction_confirmed, confidence ≥0.5). Spec enumerates new mechanism tokens (candidates: shape_consensus, sibling_context_match — final names per spec) with priority position in the cascade and interaction with Phase 1's existing 10 rules. Phase 1's 10-rule order is preserved; new rules slot before the fallback rules unless spec rationale argues otherwise. MADR 0081 (mechanism vocabulary) updated additively to register the new tokens.

title: ac-02 floor gap: locked weights cannot reach 60%/0.7 on measure half
description: Implementation of finetype-7zi yields ~7-9% non-unknown rate at confidence ≥0.7 on the measure half of failure_log.tsv vs the 60% floor demanded by ac-02. Locked weights w_v=0.4, w_h=0.6 mean score = 0.4·v + 0.6·h cannot reach 0.7 unless validator passes ≥1.0 AND header overlap-on-min ≥0.5, OR validator ≥0.5 AND header ≥0.83. Real failure_log rows are by selection columns where the model misclassified, so neither signal often clears those bars. Calibrate (9.0%) and measure (7.6%) halves agree — no overfit. Per implementation instructions, weights are non-negotiable; either ac02_threshold needs amendment (the 0.4-0.5 range gives ~98%/24% non-unknown rates) or Phase-2 signals (generator_shape, sibling_context per spec implementation_notes line 433) need adding. Surfaced for Nightingale per the parent bead's escalation protocol.

title: Autonomous type-inference module for cycle worker
description:
Pass-2 tabletop session 2026-05-10 surfaced this as a P1 deliverable. The 2026-05-03 GitTables 90% round-trip contract's E01 escalation fired 7 times across 7 full cycles to no effect because its trigger expression assumes an inference capability the cycle worker doesn't have:

> failure_log accumulates ≥ 20 distinct (predicted_type, observed_inferred_type) pairs

All 21,789 failure-log entries from pass-1 cycles have inferred_correct_type = "unknown" — the cycle worker has no autonomous module that, given a column's observed values + predicted (incorrect) type, infers what the *real* type should be. Without that, the (predicted, inferred) pair-structure collapses to a single-axis "20 distinct predicted_types" threshold, trivially crossed by cycle 1.

The pass-2 contract (2026-05-10-gittables-90-percent-roundtrip.yaml) splits E01 into:
- E01a — autonomous, gated on inferred_correct_type != "unknown" (STRUCTURALLY BLOCKED until this bead ships)
- E01b — calibration backstop, surfaces tabletop ask when N predicted_types accumulate without inference

Without this bead, E01a structurally cannot fire. Every retrain forever happens via E01b → human-attended tabletop. That works but is the slow path; this bead is the fast path.

Specification (skeleton; refine before implementing):
- Input: a column from a parquet file — name, predicted_type, observed values sample, optional sibling-column context
- Output: inferred_correct_type (a taxonomy type ID), confidence score, mechanism tag ("header-signal" | "value-shape" | "prefix-shape" | "sibling-context")
- Fallback: emit "unknown" with reason if confidence < threshold
- Surface: invoked from cycle worker's B01 / B02a branch handlers before failure_log append
- Constraint: must be deterministic (same inputs → same output) for cycle reproducibility
- Constraint: must run in <100ms per column on M1 to stay within cycle budget

Acceptance:
- ac-01: a clear specification document exists naming the candidate approach (e.g. retrieval over taxonomy generators + value-shape match, or a small classifier head trained on the harvest_pool, or rule-based first then learned later)
- ac-02: implementation produces non-"unknown" inferred_correct_type on at least 60% of B01 entries from the existing harvest_pool (21,789 entries) at confidence ≥ 0.7
- ac-03: cycle worker integration: B01 / B02a branch handlers call the module before failure_log append; mechanism tag is recorded
- ac-04: deterministic: rerun on identical inputs produces byte-identical output
- ac-05: <100ms per column on M1 (measured median over 1000 columns)
- ac-06: smoke test wired into cycle preamble — module loads, sanity-infers one canned column, returns expected type

Related:
- 2026-05-10-gittables-90-percent-roundtrip.yaml (the contract this unblocks)
- 2026-05-10-pass2-tabletop-brief.md (the audit that surfaced this)
- harvest_pool.tsv has 21,789 real B01/B02-candidate entries with "unknown" inferred_correct_type — fertile training/test data for whatever approach lands

Filed by pass-2 tabletop session 2026-05-10.
design:
# Design: Autonomous type-inference module for cycle worker

**Date:** 2026-05-04
**Interviewer:** Nightingale
**Bead:** finetype-7zi (P1 — bead serves as card per bead-native flow)
**Spec output:** `orbit/specs/2026-05-04-autonomous-type-inference/`

---

## Context

**Bead summary:** P1 deliverable surfaced in 2026-05-10 pass-2 tabletop. The 2026-05-03 GitTables 90% round-trip contract's E01 escalation fired 7 times across 7 full cycles to no effect because its trigger expression assumes inference capability the cycle worker doesn't have:

> failure_log accumulates ≥ 20 distinct (predicted_type, observed_inferred_type) pairs

All 21,789 failure_log entries from pass-1 cycles have `inferred_correct_type = "unknown"`. The pass-2 contract split E01 into E01a (autonomous, structurally blocked until this bead ships) and E01b (calibration backstop, human-attended tabletop). Without 7zi every retrain forever happens via E01b.

**Prior specs (closest matches by topic):**
- `orbit/cards/0014-profile-validate-precision.yaml` — precision card, parent context
- `orbit/cards/0015-status-orderid-misclassification.yaml` (status: proposed, no specs yet) — same misclassification family (status→periodicity, order_id→SEDOL); proposes training-data-side fix path
- `orbit/decisions/0075-mechanism-bucket-coalesce.md` — established 4-bucket / 6-trigger cascade for `validate-corpus` mechanism attribution; cascade takes (predicted, expected, samples) → mechanism
- `orbit/decisions/0078-validator-alternations-compose-canonical-sibling-patterns.md` — composition-over-invention doctrine; validators are canonical pattern source

**Architectural insight surfaced during design:** This inference module is the *forward direction* of the MADR 0075 cascade — same discrimination axis (validator-broken / subtype-drift / model-error), but inferring the unknown `expected` rather than explaining a known `(predicted, expected)` pair.

**Gap to close:** Cycle worker writes `inferred_correct_type = "unknown"` at `scripts/cron_cycle_work.py:382, 410`. Need module that fills this column with a real taxonomy ID (or a justified fallback) plus a mechanism tag, deterministically, in <100ms per column.

---

## Q&A

### Q1: Mechanism tag vocabulary
**Q:** Which mechanism vocabulary should the inference module emit — bead's (header-signal / value-shape / prefix-shape / sibling-context), MADR 0075's existing cascade vocabulary, or hybrid?
**A:** Hugh did not pick from the offered options; pushed back on the framing. Pointed out via titanic and airports examples that **validators are NOT always orthogonal ground truth**. Sex column rejects 891/891 because `identity.person.gender` enum is case-sensitive and incomplete. timezone column rejects 6761/7698 because `datetime.offset.iana` enum has 12 entries vs ~600 IANA zones. Name column rejects 177/891 because the regex disallows parentheses. The validators themselves can be the broken signal.

This pushback re-shaped Q1: the question isn't vocabulary, it's whether the module is sophisticated enough to *distinguish* validator-broken from model-error. The 0075 cascade already encodes that discrimination. Implication: align with 0075 vocabulary because the cascade IS the discrimination architecture, not just a label set. Confirmed via Q3 answer (triangulator architecture).

### Q2: Calibration target
**Q:** Is ac-02 (≥60% non-unknown at confidence ≥0.7) a floor (optimise upward) or a target (calibrate to that exact corner)?
**A:** **60%/0.7 is a floor — optimise upward (Recommended).** Hit the AC, then push higher-precision subset at higher confidence. Empirical sweep against harvest_pool determines the achievable corner. Spec progress reports both numbers.

### Q3: Architectural premise
**Q:** Given validators are themselves error-prone, what's the inference module's stance toward the model's prediction — from-scratch type-finder, triangulator over multiple signals, confirm-or-deny, or validator-audit-first?
**A:** **Triangulator over multiple signals (Recommended).** Fuse validator pass-rate + generator-shape + header signal + sibling-context. Use model's prediction as structural prior. Output mechanism distinguishes validator-broken / subtype-drift / model-error. Naturally aligns with MADR 0075's cascade vocabulary.

### Q4: Validator authority
**Q:** When the module concludes the validator (not the model) is the problem, what authority does it have?
**A:** **Read-only signal: emit mechanism = `validator_widening`, no automated fix (Recommended).** Module flags the case. Cycle worker logs it. Human review (or future bead) decides whether to amend the validator. Stays inside the contract's halt/escalation framework via E04 (taxonomy amendment) which is already manual-attended.

### Q5: Fallback policy
**Q:** When no taxonomy validator scores well on a column, what does the module emit — generic fallback, strict unknown, or cascade?
**A:** **Generic fallback with low confidence (Recommended).** Emit `representation.text.string` (or closest generic) at confidence ~0.3-0.5. Rationale: "unknown" should mean "I cannot read this column" (empty/null/garbage), not "I read it but no canonical type fits". Keeps E01a viable for genuinely-novel shapes.

### Q6: B02 scope
**Q:** Does this bead change MADR 0078 policy on B02-candidate logging, or stay narrowly on B01/B04?
**A:** **Stay on B01/B04 only (Recommended).** Inference module fills `inferred_correct_type` for entries the cycle worker already logs. Does not change which branches log. B02-candidate logging is a separate decision deserving its own card.

### Q7: Phase 1 signals
**Q:** Which of the four triangulator signals must Phase 1 ship — validator pass-rate, header-name, generator-shape, sibling-context — to satisfy ac-02?
**A:** **Validator pass-rate + header-name (Recommended).** Cheap pair. Enough for the Sex/timezone/order_id/status cases. Fits the <100ms budget easily. Generator-shape and sibling-context become Phase 2 levers if 60%/0.7 isn't met empirically.

---

## Summary

### Goal

Ship a deterministic, autonomous type-inference module that fills `failure_log.tsv`'s `inferred_correct_type` column with a meaningful taxonomy ID (or principled fallback) plus a mechanism tag, so that E01a in the 2026-05-10 GitTables 90% round-trip contract can fire on real (predicted, inferred) pair-distinctness instead of degenerating to "20 distinct predicted types".

### Constraints

- **Deterministic.** Same inputs → byte-identical output (ac-04).
- **<100ms per column on M1**, median over 1000 columns (ac-05).
- **Phase 1 signals limited to validator pass-rate + header-name match.** Defer generator-shape and sibling-context unless calibration sweep shows they're needed to hit ≥60%/0.7.
- **Read-only on the taxonomy.** Inference may flag `validator_widening` as a mechanism but does not auto-amend definitions. E04 remains human-attended.
- **Stay on B01/B04 logging surfaces.** Do not extend to B02-candidates in this bead. MADR 0078 policy unchanged.
- **Mechanism vocabulary aligned with MADR 0075's cascade buckets** (`format_diversity`, `code_vs_canonical`, `enum_overfit`, `misclassification`) extended with inference-specific labels (`validator_widening`, `prediction_confirmed`, etc.) where the cascade vocabulary doesn't cover the case.
- **Triangulator architecture, not from-scratch type-finder.** Use the model's prediction as a structural prior; output mechanism explains agreement or disagreement with that prior.
- **Generic fallback policy.** When no validator scores well, emit `representation.text.string` at low confidence (≈0.3-0.5). Reserve `unknown` for genuinely unreadable columns.

### Success Criteria

- ac-01: spec doc names "triangulator over validator pass-rate + header-name match (Phase 1)" as the candidate approach
- ac-02: ≥60% non-unknown `inferred_correct_type` on harvest_pool's 21,789 B01/B04 entries at confidence ≥0.7 — **this is a floor, not a target**; report achievable (non_unknown_rate, confidence) curve
- ac-03: B01 (lines 376-391) and B04 (lines 403-418) handlers in `scripts/cron_cycle_work.py` call the module before failure_log append; mechanism tag recorded in existing `mechanism` column
- ac-04: deterministic — golden-input regression test in cycle preamble or unit-test layer
- ac-05: <100ms median per column, M1, over 1000-column benchmark
- ac-06: smoke test wired into `scripts/cron_preamble.sh` — module loads, sanity-infers one canned column, returns expected type

### Decisions Surfaced

These need MADR records during/after the spec phase:

- **D1 — Triangulator architecture for autonomous inference.** Chose multi-signal fusion (validator pass-rate + header + sibling + generator) using model prediction as prior, over (a) from-scratch validator-retrieval, (b) confirm-or-deny binary, (c) validator-audit-first split. Rationale: titanic/airports evidence shows validator pass-rate alone confuses validator-broken with model-error. Triangulator is the smallest architecture that distinguishes the three failure modes.
- **D2 — Read-only validator authority.** Inference module flags `validator_widening` as a mechanism but does not auto-amend definitions. Validator widening remains human-attended via E04 and tabletop. Deferred even with high-confidence widening proposals — risk of taxonomy drift outweighs throughput gain.
- **D3 — Mechanism vocabulary aligned with MADR 0075 cascade buckets.** Re-use `format_diversity` / `code_vs_canonical` / `enum_overfit` / `misclassification`. Extend with inference-specific labels (`validator_widening`, `enum_completeness`, `prediction_confirmed`, `subtype_drift`, `unknown_no_fit`) where 0075 doesn't cover. Avoids parallel-vocabulary drift.
- **D4 — Generic fallback policy.** `representation.text.string` at confidence ≈0.3 when no validator passes well. `unknown` reserved for empty/null/garbage columns.
- **D5 — Phase 1 ships validator-pass-rate + header-name only.** Generator-shape and sibling-context deferred. Empirical sweep determines whether Phase 2 is needed.
- **D6 — B01/B04 only; B02-candidate logging unchanged.** MADR 0078 policy stands.

### Implementation Notes

Means-level observations from codebase exploration — starting context for the implementing agent:

- **Append sites in cycle worker:** `scripts/cron_cycle_work.py` lines 376-391 (B01) and 403-418 (B04) are structurally identical — both build a failure_row dict with hardcoded `"inferred_correct_type": "unknown"` and `"mechanism": "value-shape"`. Refactor into a single `_infer_and_append_failure_row()` helper that calls the inference module.
- **Existing primitives in Rust:**
  - `crates/finetype-core/src/validator.rs` (48KB) — already loaded by the runtime as "240 validators cached, 6 with locale validators". Pre-compiled, ready to call.
  - `crates/finetype-core/src/taxonomy.rs` (55KB) — 240 type definitions, including labels usable for header-name match.
  - `crates/finetype-core/src/generator.rs` (306KB) — Phase 2 lever for generator-shape signal; not needed in Phase 1.
- **Surface recommendation:** Rust binary subcommand `finetype infer` reading JSON from stdin (`{column_name, predicted_type, samples, [siblings]}`) and returning JSON to stdout (`{inferred_correct_type, confidence, mechanism, signals: {...}}`). Cycle worker (Python) shells out per column.
  - **Latency caveat:** subprocess fork + JSON serialisation may breach 100ms on small columns. If empirical measurement shows it does, escalate to a long-lived `finetype infer-server` (Unix socket) started from `scripts/cron_preamble.sh`. Decide empirically — start with subprocess.
  - The validator runtime already loads in `finetype validate`; reusing the loader for `finetype infer` keeps cold-start cost amortised by the cycle preamble.
- **Header-match heuristic:** taxonomy label IDs (`identity.person.gender`, `datetime.offset.iana`) decompose into bigrams that match column-name normalised tokens. Lightweight string-distance + token-set Jaccard. No ML needed in Phase 1.
- **Validator pass-rate signal:** for each candidate type, run its validator over the observed samples; record pass count / sample count. Top-k candidates feed downstream scoring.
- **Score fusion:** weighted sum or rank-aggregated (Borda count) over the two phase-1 signals. Confidence = max-signal-agreement. Specifics determined by calibration sweep.
- **failure_log schema is additive-friendly.** Existing columns: cycle_id, timestamp, file_path, file_content_sha256, column_name, predicted_type, observed_values_sample, **inferred_correct_type** (gets filled), **mechanism** (gets richer vocabulary), confidence (NEW — append column).
- **Calibration corpus:** `eval/gittables/failure_log.tsv` (21,789 rows). Run inference module against the unlabelled rows, sweep confidence threshold, report (non_unknown_rate, threshold) curve. See Open Question §1 for ground-truth gap.
- **Smoke test (ac-06):** add a canned-input invocation to `scripts/cron_preamble.sh` after the existing model-load check. Input: a fixture column from `eval/datasets/csv/titanic.csv` (Sex). Expected output: `inferred_correct_type=identity.person.gender`, mechanism includes `enum_overfit` or `validator_widening`. Failing the canned input halts the cycle (H05 family).

### Open Questions

Intent-level only — implementation questions resolved in spec phase.

1. **Ground-truth gap for ac-02 measurement.** failure_log's 21,789 rows are unlabelled. Without a hand-labelled subset (200-500 entries), the calibration sweep can measure non_unknown_rate but not whether the inferences are *correct*. ac-02's "60% non-unknown at confidence ≥0.7" measures the module's decisiveness, not its accuracy. Spec phase must answer: does the bead's acceptance want decisiveness, or does it want labelled-precision? If the latter, scope expands to include labelling. Recommendation to surface in spec: hand-label 200 entries during implementation and report precision-on-labelled alongside non_unknown_rate-on-full.

2. **Confidence units across signals.** Validator pass-rate is a fraction in [0, 1]. Header-name match is a string-distance score in [0, 1]. They're not commensurate. The fusion weights and the meaning of "confidence ≥0.7" depend on the chosen aggregation. Recommendation: spec phase prescribes the aggregation (weighted sum vs rank-aggregation vs lexicographic) before the bead lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] ac-01: spec doc names "triangulator over validator pass-rate + header-name match (Phase 1)" as approach
- [x] ac-02: ≥5% non-unknown inferred_correct_type on measure half of failure_log.tsv at confidence ≥0.7 with locked weights w_v=0.4, w_h=0.6 (recalibrated from 60% per MADR 0084; empirical: 7.1%)
- [x] ac-03: B01/B04 helper refactor in cron_cycle_work.py removes hardcoded "unknown"/"value-shape"; sidecar row written per column
- [x] ac-04 [gate]: deterministic — lex iteration at scoring + round-to-4dp before argmax + lex tie-break; 100-round sub-ulp stress test stable
- [x] ac-05 [gate]: <100ms median per column on M1 over 1000-column benchmark using production code path
- [x] ac-06 [gate]: smoke test in cron_preamble.sh — canonical email column (identity.person.email), mechanism == prediction_confirmed, confidence ≥0.5, halts cycle on failure
- [x] ac-07: weighted-sum score(type) = w_v · validator_pass_rate + w_h · header_match; weights LOCKED at w_v=0.4, w_h=0.6 (no agent-driven sweep)

- [x] ac-09: closed mechanism vocabulary (10 tokens) — 7 from MADR 0075 rule-emitted set + 3 triangulator extensions; precondition guard for empty samples + 9-rule deterministic cascade
- [x] ac-10: fallback policy — Rule 1 (max_score < fallback_threshold=0.4) emits text.string@0.3 + unknown_no_fit; precondition (empty samples) emits unknown@0.0 + fallthrough
- [x] ac-11: Phase 1 signal scope locked to validator pass-rate + header-name match
- [x] ac-12: sidecar inference_signals.tsv created (12 cols, append-only); failure_log.tsv 9-col schema unchanged; FULL OUTER JOIN audit on (cycle_id, file_path, sha, column_name) over 3-cycle window
- [x] ac-13: 200-row labelled_eval.tsv from measure half only; labelling_protocol.md documents rubric; precision-on-labelled reported

E01a unblocked. Phase 2 (generator-shape + sibling-context) filed as finetype-7zi.3 with empirical anchor (precision-on-labelled finding).

title: launchd plist for cron-firing FineType agent
description:
Infrastructure precondition for autonomy-contract activation. The active contract at orbit/contracts/2026-05-03-gittables-90-percent-roundtrip.yaml requires the cron-firing agent to run unattended on macOS every 2h (per §1 cycle cadence + §2 standing orders).

Local CronCreate is REPL-bound; launchd is the right mechanism.

## Specification

See docs/CRON-LAUNCHD-SETUP.md for the full self-contained spec — that document is the authoritative handoff for whoever picks up this work. Summary:

- launchd plist at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/online.meridian.finetype-cron.plist
- Triggers: every 2h (StartInterval 7200, or StartCalendarInterval array)
- Invocation: `claude -p "<contract-cycle-prompt>"` with appropriate working directory + env
- Lockfile coordination: respects /tmp/finetype-cron.lock from finetype-nms
- Logging: stdout + stderr to ~/Library/Logs/finetype-cron/ rotated daily
- Disable mechanism: `launchctl unload` + plist removal documented for emergency stop
- Survives system reboot (launchd default behaviour, unlike CronCreate which dies with REPL)

## Acceptance

description:
Promoted from: orbit/cards/0011-agent-ready-skills.yaml

Goal: Two skills shipped (/finetype-pipeline, /finetype-cli) — agents complete full pipeline, not just profile

## Current state (cycle 3)

Both skills already exist on disk:
- .claude/skills/finetype-pipeline/SKILL.md (3-step pipeline correctly described, no behavioural-fixture artefact)
- .claude/skills/finetype-cli/SKILL.md (banner stale at v0.6.12; multiple flag-level divergences from the v0.6.19 binary surface)

2. Add a standalone drift-check script (`scripts/verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh`) that diffs the skill inventory against the live `finetype --help` surface.

title: Cron-firing agent: standardise long-running launcher idiom
description:
Cycle df6a4260 (2026-05-03 ~13:39Z) failed mid-flight. Symptoms:

1. The cron-firing agent's first attempt wrapped gate + work commands in `nohup ... &` inside a Bash run_in_background:true call. The wrapper bash exited 0 immediately; the agent took the exit code as completion and launched fresh duplicates — without the inner nohup-detached process being visible to ps from the agent's next check.

2. Three concurrent cron_cycle_work.py processes ended up writing to the same append-only logs under cycle_id df6a4260 before the agent pkill'd them. Append-integrity is intact (fcntl.flock + O_APPEND), but the cycle_id is reused across partial overlapping writes, totalling 524 coverage rows + 446 failure rows + 446 harvest rows.

3. The gate measurement was never run to completion this cycle.

Recovery: cycle ended via H02 + unmatched_state_partial_cycle_data escalation. Cycle log entry written; lockfile released. Next cycle (~15:39Z if launchd cadence holds) will start fresh with shifted visit_counts.

This bead asks the next tabletop to settle the canonical launcher idiom so future cycles don't repeat. Candidate solutions:
- Always launch via `Bash run_in_background:true` with the actual command (no nohup/&). The Bash tool reparents to launchd when its parent exits, but the process keeps running and the tool reports completion when it exits.
- Document a wait-then-verify pattern: after launching, ps -ef | grep -F "<cycle_id>" to confirm the process is alive before considering further actions.
- Have scripts/cron_cycle.sh write a per-run pidfile alongside the lockfile so the agent has an authoritative source for "is the worker still running".

Filed under finetype-cron because it's an infrastructure delta on top of the autonomy-contract activation beads (e6d/s16/87j/nms/53r).

title: Fix scripts/gittables_gate.sh empty-array crash on bash 3.2
description:
Cycle ba3bea78 attempted to invoke 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' with no args (the wrapper's nominal default per its docstring) and crashed on macOS bash 3.2:

  scripts/gittables_gate.sh: line 49: PASSTHRU[@]: unbound variable

Cause: bash 3.2 (default on macOS) errors on empty-array "${PASSTHRU[@]}" reference under 'set -u'. The wrapper's docstring promises 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' (no-arg) is a valid invocation, but it isn't on bash 3.2.

Workaround used this cycle: invoke with '--jobs 1' (any arg makes PASSTHRU non-empty). Cycles c7e7a6cc and 99de5b2c likely ran with explicit args too; their stderrs show the wrapper succeeded.

Fix: change line 49 from "${PASSTHRU[@]}" to a guarded form, e.g.:

  if (( ${#PASSTHRU[@]} > 0 )); then
      python3 scripts/gittables_gate.py "${PASSTHRU[@]}" >"$TMP_SUMMARY"
  else
      python3 scripts/gittables_gate.py >"$TMP_SUMMARY"
  fi

Or upgrade shebang to a newer bash (homebrew) — but that introduces a non-default-shell dependency the wrapper currently avoids.

Acceptance:
- [ ] 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh --max-files 2' works (already passes)
- [ ] 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' (no args) works on /bin/bash (3.2.57)
- [ ] 'cron_cycle.sh --dry-run' works on /bin/bash (the dry-run path invokes the wrapper with args, but the production path also invokes via launchd; verify both)

title: Wire verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh into release CI gate
description:
The CLI skill drift harness ships in PR #63 (finetype-u6a / card 0011) but
runs manually only — neither tests/smoke.sh nor .github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml
invokes it.

Until wired in, drift between .claude/skills/finetype-cli/SKILL.md and the live
finetype binary surface is silent. The whole point of the harness is to catch
this at release time; manual invocation defeats it.

## Scope

1. Add a CI step that runs `scripts/verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh` against the
   built binary. Pre-release gate (.github/workflows/release.yml) is the
   minimum bar; ci.yml on every PR is preferable so drift is surfaced before
   release.
2. Failure (exit 1: drift detected) blocks the release. Exit 2 (script error,
   missing binary, missing SKILL.md) also blocks — these are environment bugs
   the operator should see immediately, not silent skips.
3. Confirm FINETYPE_BIN resolves to the just-built binary (not a system
   install) so the check matches what's about to ship.

## Precedent

`.github/scripts/check-ci-model-drift.sh` is wired into CI as a non-blocking
warning (GitHub Actions `::warning::`). For this bead the gate is blocking,
since the contract is "skill matches binary on release" not advisory drift.

## Done when

- A failing run of verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh blocks PR merge or release
  publish (operator preference).
- The wiring's failure mode is visible in CI logs (not buried).
- The bead's reviewer can confirm the drift script ran during the PR's
  release-gate check.

## Out of scope

- Authoring CHECKLIST.md drift checks (CHECKLIST.md is the pipeline skill's
  behavioural artefact; no equivalent automated harness yet).
- Multi-runtime portability (Cursor / Aider / etc.) — separate bead if needed.

Surfaced from review-pr cycle 1 of finetype-u6a as deferred follow-up; AC-03
of that bead explicitly carved CI wiring out of scope.
